page: Amazon Web Services m9g.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor. It features 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) running at 3.3 GHz, with 4.0 GB of system memory. The CPU architecture is arm64, supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. This instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m9g.medium demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, particularly in data compression and decompression tasks. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 36.08 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scored in the top tier at 17.04 GB/sec. Geekbench single-core testing also shows strong results with a score of 2223.0. However, due to its single-core configuration, multi-core and parallelized workloads show poor relative performance, as reflected in a multi-core Geekbench score of 2207.0 and a poor multi-core stress-ng rating. Memory bandwidth is moderate, with large-block read speeds averaging 43.27 GB/sec, though write speeds and small-block cached reads are relatively weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m9g.medium offers a low-cost entry point into the ARM64 Graviton ecosystem, providing dedicated CPU resources without the burstable credit limitations of shared-core instances. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads such as basic web serving, text processing, simple scripting, and development or testing environments. It is less suitable for database operations, multi-threaded compilation, or memory-intensive applications due to its 4.0 GB memory limit and single-vCPU constraint.
